title: Introduce cacheable toolchain wrapper and fast presubmit prober
author: Lena Hoffman
release_notes: Adds a cached, hermetic toolchain wrapper to speed presubmit boot and a lightweight presubmit prober for faster feedback; no user-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: presubmit latency is a major drag on developer iteration. Cold presubmit setup (installing language toolchains, devdeps) adds minutes to feedback time and increases flakiness from transient network failures. Goal: provide a small, cacheable toolchain wrapper that produces deterministic build environments and a fast presubmit prober that exercises only the minimal smoke surface to detect obvious breakages quickly. This PR implements: 1) tools/toolchain-wrapper: a Go-based thin wrapper that normalizes tool versions, creates a local small cache image and exposes a simple wrapper CLI (redwood-tw) to run builds/tests hermetically; it supports a disk-backed cache artifact (tarball) and a lightweight HTTP cache server for CI runners. 2) .github/workflows/presubmit.yml: adds a presubmit fast-path job that uses the toolchain wrapper and runs the new prober job. 3) ci/presubmit-prober: a tiny Go binary that runs language-heuristic smoke checks (go vet, pytests targeted by quick tags, ts compile) and reports structured pass/fail to the checks API. 4) Scripts and Dockerfile.toolcache to build and snapshot a small toolcache image that can be reused across CI runners. Rollout plan: landing as opt-in under feature flag ci.fast-presubmit; we will run the new prober in parallel to existing presubmit for two weeks, collect failure-mode telemetry and then switch to fast-path by default. Backwards compatibility: the wrapper falls back to the legacy bootstrap when the toolcache is unavailable. Checklist: [x] unit tests for wrapper cache eviction [x] prober smoke tests [x] updated docs and README for wrapper usage [x] feature-flag gating and telemetry. Related: references ENG-4251 for presubmit SLO work and SUP-3112 for a recent customer incident caused by flaky devdep installs. See design notes at https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4251/details.
commits: Add cache server and tarball snapshot logic
Presubmit prober implementation and smoke tests
CI workflow changes: add fast-presubmit lane and caching steps
Fix: handle private registries and secure token propagation
Docs: usage, rollout notes and debug guide
review_comments: Marcus: Can we avoid leaking registry auth into the cache snapshot? Added suggestion to use token vaulted via CI secrets.

Evan: Noted a flaky test on macOS runner; requested we skip that probe for macOS until follow-up.

notes_on_rollout: Feature gated under ci.fast-presubmit. Ops: bake toolcache image into runner pool and enable the fast path for non-release branches initially. Monitor presubmit latency SLO and cache hit rate. Revert plan: flip flag off and CI falls back to legacy bootstrap; notify oncall infra if cache server errors exceed threshold.
post_merge_tasks: Publish toolcache image to internal registry
Create ENG-4295 to stabilize macOS probes
Schedule a 2-week parallel run and collect telemetry
safety_and_security: The cache tarball is stored in internal bucket; snapshot creation requires ci-toolkit service role. We added safeguards: content signing of tarball, short-lived upload tokens, and an allowlist for external registries. No secrets are stored in snapshots; registry credentials are redacted and replaced with ephemeral fetchers.
testing_and_monitoring: Added unit coverage for cache eviction, prober tests that simulate common failure modes, and a presubmit telemetry event (presubmit.prober.latency) that will be consumed by the CI SLO dashboards.
